panels.title: More attackers, greater success
panels.subtitle: CIFAR-10 · ResNet-18 · 10 clients
panels.finding: More malicious clients raised every attack’s mean ASR; invisible attacks remained below BadNet in both settings.

panels.title: Attention placement has a cost
panels.subtitle: LSB700 · CIFAR-10 · 10% attackers
panels.finding: Low-attention placement reaches 61.39% ASR, while anomaly index rises to 3.04, above the discussed detection threshold of 2.

takeaways: Attacker participation matters: all tested attacks gain success as more clients are compromised.
Placement changes the tradeoff: low-attention LSB700 gains 19.80 pp ASR, with greater distortion and detectability.

locations: Table 1, PDF page 10 (including repository cover): all five attacks, ASR at 10% and 20% malicious clients.
Table 3, PDF page 14: LSB700 no-mask, low-attention and high-attention rows; ASR, LPIPS and anomaly index.
Section 5.3, PDF pages 14–15: LSB attention-placement scope and anomaly-threshold discussion.

notes: Visually checked original pages 10, 11 and 14 using digests/scratch-privacy/2024-fiba/page-010.png, page-011.png and page-014.png; cross-checked text and PDF SHA-256.

All five Table 1 attacks remain in source order. The paired chart shows mean ASR, preserving each original ± string in labels. Direction is null because ASR describes attack effectiveness, not a desirable defense outcome.
The paper does not identify its ± statistic or repetition count. Do not label error values as standard deviations or confidence intervals, or claim statistical significance.
Supporting table uses the three existing LSB700 insight rows in their established order. Exact improvement is 61.39 - 41.59 = 19.80 percentage points; it is not a relative-percent improvement.
FiBA is a benchmark of invisible federated backdoors. The attention-placement evidence is LSB500/700; no frequency-domain mechanism is inferred.
Low-attention LSB700 increases LPIPS from 7.83 × 10^-5 to 2.25 × 10^-4 and anomaly from 1.61 to 3.04. The smaller LSB500 ASR gain (24.72 - 20.17 = 4.55 pp) prevents generalizing the 19.80 pp result.
Table 2 defense grid is omitted from this two-panel selection rather than pooled across datasets and attacker fractions. No universal defense-evasion claim is made.
Source is the TU/e accepted manuscript with repository cover, not the publisher typeset version; page anchors count the cover.
